assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing turns a defined chemical reaction (hydrolytic cytidine deamination, later engineered adenosine deamination) into a programmable, general tool for changing a single nucleotide without a double-strand break. It is chemically precise, mechanistically transparent and has transformed genome-maintenance and disease-variant research; clinical use is already under way. From my vantage, the strength is the clean enzymology behind the tool.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the intellectual driver and the lab that conceived both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead experimentalists on the two editors. Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID) were close parallel work, so credit is not fully unambiguous, and a prize with Liu alone or Liu plus the CRISPR founders' prior recognition is also conceivable.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in a very large number of laboratories and in animals and human clinical trials within about a decade; the interpretation is stable. Timing is arguably ripe, though recognition of CRISPR-Cas9 in 2020 may lead some to wait.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views base editing as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Credit relative to Nishida and Kondo's concurrent Target-AID work.
Long-term off-target and bystander editing profile is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes small-molecule pharmacology: a bifunctional or glue molecule hijacks an E3 ligase to destroy a chosen protein. The chemical concept (induced proximity, event-driven rather than occupancy-driven action) is original, general and already yielding clinical compounds. The mechanism of thalidomide acting through cereblon is a satisfying piece of chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underlies molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later contributions, and the list is crowded, so a three-person split is contested and somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, many compounds in clinical trials, but no approved PROTAC drug that I can confirm and clinical benefit is not yet proven. Slightly early for medical validation but the chemistry is well established.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between PROTAC concept, cereblon discovery and molecular glue work.
I cannot independently verify current clinical status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles solved the delivery problem for siRNA and mRNA medicines through a chemical principle: lipids that are neutral in circulation and charged in the acidified endosome. The impact is concrete and very large, including the first siRNA drug and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. It is a real chemistry-of-medicine invention rather than a biological observation.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the ionizable-lipid LNP formulation concept and manufacturing; MacLachlan led the translation into siRNA and Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries and screening. Hope and Madden were early co-inventors. The credit is diffuse and any three will leave out strong claimants.
assessment.maturity: Extensively validated at population scale. Timing is good, although the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA modifications may be seen as having covered part of the territory.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution across a decades-long academic and industrial effort.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine recognition of mRNA vaccines.
Patent and industrial priority issues are outside my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids at defined sites using orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It converts translation into a controllable chemical platform for biochemists: photocrosslinkers, labels and post-translational mimics in living cells. It is original, general and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang introduced the first orthogonal pair in living cells and the general approach; Chin extended it to higher organisms and to multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama made important contributions. A Schultz, Chin, Wang configuration is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely reproduced for more than twenty years, with many users. Timing is fully ripe.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would give priority to the method over its applications.
Relative credit of Yokoyama and Mehl.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made routine, automated, high-yield synthesis of defined DNA possible, and it underlies PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis, oligonucleotide therapeutics and much of molecular biology. As someone who works with nucleotides, I regard it as foundational chemistry that others built on.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method itself; Hood's role was in the automated synthesizer instrument and is less central to the chemical discovery. A single laureate, or Caruthers with a coauthor, is reasonable.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of unambiguous validation; the question is only why the prize has not come sooner. Not premature, perhaps a late recognition.
uncertainties: Whether earlier contributions, such as Letsinger's phosphite-triester work, complicate sole credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, particularly sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators, turned nucleotide chemistry into a technology that reshaped genomics and medicine. The chemical core, reversible terminator nucleotides and clustered amplification, is elegant and has an unparalleled breadth of impact.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded Solexa chemistry; Rothberg led 454 pyrosequencing-based parallel sequencing. Mayer and Ju contributed alternative approaches. The credit is entangled with company histories, and the field's chemistry versus engineering split is ambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with enormous independent adoption. The 1980 sequencing prize and later nanopore and long-read work create overlap questions.
uncertainties: Attribution is a mixture of chemistry, instrumentation and commercial development.
Whether a Chemistry prize is natural or whether this is closer to a Medicine or Physiology theme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics allows quantitative, system-wide measurement of proteins and their modifications, which for a quantitative biochemist is the analogous capability to dNTP-pool measurement. Its impact on biology and biomarker research is substantial and sustained.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the leading figures in methods (shotgun proteomics, SRM, quantitative approaches). Hunt, Gygi and Heck also have strong claims, so any trio omits other legitimate contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used, though the 2002 Chemistry prize for ionization of biomolecules already recognised the enabling technology, which raises a question of sufficient novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 recognition of biomolecular mass spectrometry.
Quantification accuracy and reproducibility across platforms remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase structure and mechanism tackles one of the hardest enzymatic reactions in nature, the reduction of dinitrogen at an FeMo cofactor with a central carbide. Mechanistic questions parallel those in radical enzymes such as ribonucleotide reductase, and the problem is of fundamental chemical and agricultural importance.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural determination of the protein and cofactor; Einsle solved the central carbide structure at high resolution; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanistic and biochemical work, and Ribbe's group the cofactor biosynthesis and reconstitution. A fair configuration is possible but difficult.
assessment.maturity: The structure is firmly established but the catalytic mechanism is still debated; the discovery may be premature as a mechanism prize.
uncertainties: The reaction mechanism of N2 reduction is not fully resolved.
Credit among five groups is hard to allocate.
